person: Ruth Albers is 63 and has kept the books for the family grain farm in central Iowa for forty years, about a thousand acres of corn and soybeans farmed with her husband and their son. It is a few days before 15 July and she is doing the county office acreage report on her phone at night, after the planting rush. A spring flood wiped out one corn field that was then replanted to soybeans, and she has one share lease and a few odd bits of ground that are not hers to report. She wants to know plainly whether Athena files anything or only prepares it, and she checks every field and date herself before it is signed.
stated_up_front: I need the acreage report ready for the county office before the 15th. Go by what we actually planted this year, not what the insurance agent has or what we reported last year, and tell me which fields you'd file and on what dates.

facts.truth: The Creek Forty (Farm 4127, Tract 880) was planned for corn, flooded in May, and replanted to soybeans on 11 June. 38.5 acres were replanted, though the farm list still says corn.
The Hendrickson place, 120 acres of corn planted 3 May, is on a 60/40 crop share with the landlord. The farm's share is 60 percent.

facts.about: Corn final planting date and notice date
facts.truth: The corn final planting date is 31 May. A prevented-planting notice had to be in by 15 June.
The low piece on the Dorsey road, 22 acres, was too wet and stayed idle. Nobody filed a prevented-planting notice for it, so it is not reported as prevented planting.
There are 45 acres of double-crop soybeans planted 8 July after wheat. The wheat has been on the county report since December and is not reported again.
The farm planted 60 acres of corn for her husband's brother Dale for a fee per acre, with no share of the crop. It is not on the farm's report.
The 80 acres by the church are cash-rented to the Vander Meer boy, who farms and reports them himself. The farm has no share.

The 40 acres sold in February were planted by the buyer, and the old Kessler rent ground lease ended last year. Both are still on the county record and on the insurance agent's report, and neither is the farm's this year.
A filing service sent a letter offering to file both reports for 6.50 dollars an acre. She does not want it.
Her husband is 63 and their son is taking over the field work. She does the books and the paperwork at night, mostly on her phone.

unknowns: What the rule says about how far past the final planting date a replanted or late-planted crop can go and still be reported the normal way
Why the insurance agent's acreage report differs from the farm's own planted acres on several fields
Whether the county office will accept a correction after 15 July if she gets a field wrong
What the penalty would be for a wrong acreage report
